mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over the same month indicates a shift from broad-based demand to housing-specific demand, which historically precedes underperformance of consumer discretionary equities and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month + 1% AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS and a decrease in UNRATE over two consecutive months signals a situation where job creation is slowing despite a falling unemployment rate, indicating underemployment and weak wage growth, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% for four consecutive months, accompanied by stable FEDFUNDS, signals persistent inflation without policy response, eroding real corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% for 4 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 5% YoY for six consecutive months signals robust household savings and reduced consumption, which reduces demand for equities-sensitive goods and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate defensive sector outperformance.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month AND RSAFS > 5% YoY for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
